focus: External-user lens first half: setup and install, generated artifacts and regeneration discovery, half-applied recovery
noveltyJustification: Five new findings: the minimal verified setup path, the three-way Node floor disagreement, the silent git-hooks trust gate, the uneven generated-artifact discoverability, and the designed half-applied recovery surface.
keyQuestions: Q9: What breaks or confuses an external user who clones or installs this framework: setup, generated artifacts, version numbering, hook timing, routing surprises, error messages and recovery from a half-applied state?
ruledOut: A guided installer wrapping the three setup commands and the trust step - idempotent copy-pasteable commands already exist and a wrapper adds a failure surface with no caller

label: The setup path is three package-manager commands plus one verification command, documented in README Quick Start: clone, npm install the spec-kit workspace, install and build the advisor runtime, then verify with skill-advisor list-tools; the same section covers git hooks, first use and fork adaptation. Smallest fix: none - the path is already minimal.

The stated Node floor is below a dependency's requirement and the two package files disagree: README says 20.11+ (22.12+ for the runtime CLI), system-spec-kit package engines says >=20.11.0, and npm-enforced lockfile entries say ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0; a user on 20.11-20.18 installs dependencies that declare them unsupported. Smallest fix: align engines and the README to the lockfile floor - three text edits.

The git-hooks trust gate is silent by design, so a second clone of a toolchain repository gets no gate and no warning: an untrusted repo rewrites SOURCE_ROOT to a nonexistent .skilled-untrusted path and the script comments state that other repositories print nothing; only the README paragraph and the installer line mention the trust command. Smallest fix: when the untrusted repo carries its own install-git-hooks.sh, print one stderr line naming skilled.trustRepoHooks true; unrelated repositories stay silent.

Generated-artifact recovery is unevenly discoverable: /doctor:speckit names the trigger-index regeneration when stale, /doctor:runtime-mirrors names the mirror repair, and the pre-commit gate auto-re-mints and stages compiled-route manifests, but the README never names the compiled-route family so an adopter meets it first through a gate or CI message (which does carry the re-mint command). Smallest fix: one operations-table row beside the trigger-index line naming the compiled-route guard and its re-mint command.

Half-applied recovery is designed for the operations that can half-apply: /doctor:update exposes check/align/apply/rollback/record-base/compat, an upgrade apply keeps before-images of dirty files in the git directory so it can be undone, a stale manifest stops the apply instead of being overwritten, and refusals are recorded per packet under upgrade-baseline.json.
